title: MA Protocol: CT Sinuses
desc: MA workflow for performing in-office CT sinus scans: insurance/ABN, patient preparation, positioning, and scanner settings.

blocks.content: Performing the CT scan in office
CT scanning is typically done for post-treatment evaluation — after completion of antibiotic and/or steroid therapy for chronic sinusitis or nasal polyposis.
Insurance and ABN
If the patient is NOT on Medicare, confirm the in-office CT has been insurance-verified before proceeding
If the patient is not on Medicare and insurance has not been verified, have the patient sign the ABN form — located in the PDF manager in the EMR. Out-of-pocket cost is $350.

It is best practice to contact the CT insurance coordinator promptly to run the insurance first and wait for results before having the patient sign the ABN — however this can take 20–40 minutes. Communicate the wait time to the patient.
Patient preparation
Confirm with the patient when their last saline irrigation was — best if more than 24 hours before the visit. Note this in the chart.
Place the radiation protection jacket on the patient with velcro closure
Place the neck guard on the patient
Patient positioning
Seat the patient in the CT chair with their head all the way back to touch the headrest
Adjust the chair height vertically so the vertical laser line sits at the midline of the patient's face and the horizontal laser line sits 1–2 inches below the lower eyelid
Place one foam head sponge on each side of the patient's head
Strap the patient's forehead securely
CT settings
Enter the patient's MSN number as the Patient ID, along with date of birth, full name, and sex
Standard protocol: 20 seconds, 600 — image-guided setting — unless the physician directs otherwise
